key_insight: Water transport and membrane swelling in an anion exchange membrane are strongly coupled, so hydration-dependent diffusivity alone is not enough to predict behavior under water-activity gradients.
engineering_relevance: For CO2 separation membrane design, accounting for deformation and viscoelastic stress improves prediction of hydrated membrane performance and helps identify operating conditions where mechanical feedback matters.
method: Transient finite element model of water transport + mechanical deformation in Fumasep FAA-3-50
Includes concentration-dependent diffusivity, hygroscopic swelling, and nonlinear viscoelastic response
Compares uncoupled, one-way coupled, and fully coupled formulations
evidence_signal: The fully coupled model was validated against steady-state water-transport measurements across water-activity gradients and showed the best agreement at intermediate hydration levels.
watch_item: The model still treats transport as primarily diffusion-driven, so effects outside the tested hydration range or under different operating/mechanical conditions may need additional validation.
paper_title: Modeling Transport and Mechanics in Anion Exchange Membranes to Optimize Continuous CO2 Separations
